reviews.text:
In the past, I lost my pet due to medical malpractice.

The vet examined my pet based on speculation without even a physical examination, and prescribed medication that was contraindicated for that animal. I sought a second opinion, but it was too late.

I never imagined I'd lose my beloved dog in this way.

At the beginning of this year, he suffered a ligament injury, and the head veterinarian performed surgery. He recovered well afterward. However, during regular checkups, heartworm prevention, and vaccinations, I repeatedly mentioned that his leg was slightly swollen, but I was told not to worry about it, so I left it as is.

In mid-August of this year, he had bloody stools, so I took him to a nearby hospital. They said his red blood cell count was very low and that there might be cancer, so I was told to take him back to my regular vet for a CT scan.

At that time, a female veterinarian examined him first. She said his red blood cell and liver counts were bad, but stable, so she suggested an IV drip. That was the end of the IV drip for that day. However, his appetite decreased and the bloody stools continued, so a few days later I took him back to the head veterinarian. He said there was a possibility of cancer and we should do a CT scan. If a tumor was found after the CT scan, surgery would be performed immediately. However, the surgery schedule was full, so it couldn't be done until the following week. Ultimately, the CT scan and surgery were scheduled for the following week (8 days later).

Even then, I thought waiting seven days was too long, and when I asked if it could be done sooner, I was told there were other surgeries and that the numbers wouldn't get worse, which reassured me somewhat.

Eight days later, I took my dog ​​in the morning as planned, and in the afternoon, I received a call from the head veterinarian. He simply said, "Surgery is not possible, and he doesn't have long to live." My family and I were stunned.

When I actually went to pick up my dog ​​in the afternoon for an examination, I was told, "The cancer has metastasized to his liver and heart, and surgery is not possible. He won't make it to the end of the month, and there's a possibility he'll die in five days." The moment I heard that, I felt like the blood drained from my face. Why did we have to wait eight days? If the numbers were this bad, couldn't they have acted sooner? I was so angry that I couldn't find the words to express what I wanted to say. There was no apology from the head veterinarian; he simply said to bring him in for an IV drip if he seemed unwell, and the examination ended.

After that, my beloved dog seemed to be in pain every day, even struggling to breathe. We did everything we could at a nearby hospital, including blood transfusions and radiation therapy, but just as the head veterinarian predicted, my dog ​​passed away five days later.

I'm still struggling to come to terms with the fact that he died just five days after being given a terminal diagnosis. The head veterinarian never called to check on my dog's condition. All that remains is regret.

He was such a healthy dog, never sick for the past 11 years…
Why didn't I notice sooner…?
Why didn't I ask the doctor repeatedly if they could have done tests sooner…?

All I feel is regret.

I will never go to that hospital again.

If you notice anything unusual about your dog or pet's condition, I think you should get a second opinion.

I hope that fewer pet owners will have to go through the same painful experience of saying goodbye to their beloved pets.

I want my dog ​​back.

[To those considering visiting this clinic]
I am extremely dissatisfied with the treatment I received from a female doctor, Dr. Uchimura, during an emergency visit due to a post-operative infection.
What made me feel most distrustful was that she began discussing treatment options before directly examining the wound. Only after I pointed this out did she examine the wound, and after seeing the swelling, she suggested additional tests.
The explanations were generally difficult to understand; I had to ask her to repeat them three times before I finally grasped them. Furthermore, her statements regarding treatment options were vague, such as "I think you should do this," and she didn't convey what the best course of action was at all.

As a layperson, I couldn't make a judgment, which is why I asked her to "do her best, even if it costs more," but she didn't provide proper guidance and I felt like she simply dumped the decision-making responsibility on me. I would have liked a more responsible approach.

I had my cat, Fuku-kun, examined here. The vet I usually went to had closed down, so I searched on Google Maps and went to this clinic for the first time. They said he had kidney problems and only had 2-3 days, and we were scheduled to go for an IV drip the next day, but he passed away early in the morning. The doctor explained everything to me so diligently, and I am so grateful. It's been a week since then, and I still cry and cry, but I am so grateful for the doctor's diligent explanation. Thank you.

Appointments for consultations are not available.
There is a long wait.

The veterinarians and nurses are kind and friendly. However, the reception staff tend to be unfriendly.

However, the examinations are not thorough.

My cat had an abnormality and was tested, but they said there was nothing wrong. A week later, at another hospital, it was diagnosed with feline leukemia virus and an ultrasound showed a swollen abdomen.

A friend also had their cat examined here and was told there was nothing wrong, but it was later diagnosed with FIP at another hospital.

I had heard of several other cases of misdiagnosis, but I continued going for about two years, thinking it would be okay for vaccinations.

In conclusion, I think it's fine for vaccinations and grooming, but I wouldn't recommend this hospital if you suspect your cat has an illness.

It was a very strange shop.

I reserved dog food at the store and paid in advance. At that time, the staff member explained, "It will arrive in about a week, and we will contact you."

However, more than nine days passed without any contact. When I called to inquire, they said, "It's already arrived."

When I asked, "If it's arrived, why didn't you contact me?", they flatly replied, "We have no obligation to contact customers."

Furthermore, when I asked, "What happens to this product if I don't contact you for a year?", they immediately answered, "We'll leave it there."

I was surprised by their response—they promised to contact me when it arrived, but then later said they had no obligation to do so.

I've used many different shops before, but this is the first time I've experienced such treatment. It was a very memorable, and in a way, very unique shop.

The doctor who treated me was very attentive and listened carefully to my concerns, and answered all my questions thoroughly, which put me at ease.

However, I must say, and I apologize for comparing it to other hospitals, that their queuing system is terrible. You have to register at the hospital, and waiting for over an hour is commonplace. Not only was the wait for the consultation long, but the wait for payment was almost an hour as well, which was awful.

This hospital only sees patients as cash cows. The treatment was sloppy, and even after six months of visits, they couldn't find the cause of the illness.

I trusted them because I was referred there, but since it wasn't getting any better, I looked for another hospital.

At the new hospital I found, the doctor just looked at my pet's face and said, "Its jaw is dislocated," which shocked me.

The doctor seemed hesitant to say it, but then asked, "Are there any veterinarians who overlook this?"

He also said that the treatment I had received was sloppy.

Now, things are improving at the new doctor's, so I'm relieved, but honestly, I feel like I've been scammed.

I have lots of pets at home,
small animals, amphibians, reptiles, and cats—all of them.
I take them in for checkups whenever something happens. 🍀*゜
The doctor is kind, and the nurses are kind too.
I'm always grateful.

I went there on the recommendation of my regular vet. I was a little worried after reading some reviews, but the doctor (a young woman named Dr. U) was great! She explained everything thoroughly and it was very easy to understand. She also spoke to my dog ​​with a smile, which made me feel very at ease. There was also a nurse who called my dog's name and led him to the examination room (she guided us there and asked a few quick questions about his symptoms), and there were about three receptionists, and they were all very nice.

My Super Max Snow leopard gecko is a patient here. I took him in for an examination because I was worried about his anorexia and egg binding.

I called ahead and confirmed they see reptiles, and I was reassured that they see people on a first-come, first-served basis, so I went right away.

After an ultrasound and X-ray, they explained that his egg sac was developing and causing abdominal congestion, which was leading to his anorexia, but that it was due to a calcium deficiency needed for shell formation. Their clear explanation made this a very helpful hospital for reptile beginners.

I apologize for the late review; it was three years ago.

My two-year-old cat fell from the 7th floor of our apartment building and suffered a comminuted fracture of the pelvis, so we sought their care. Immediately after the accident, we went to a small nearby animal hospital, but they couldn't handle the situation and referred us here.

The surgery took three days. They kept us updated on the situation by phone each time! We've been there several times for follow-up appointments, and it's always crowded.

The doctors seem mostly young, but each time the doctor in charge explained everything in the waiting room, which made us feel at ease.

I thought it would be expensive because it was such a sudden event, but the doctor asked me how much I was willing to pay to save her (the surgery alone was around 300,000 yen?), and when I indicated the amount I could afford, they did it for that price. What's more, she was able to walk after the surgery—it was truly a miracle! Initially, they said she might not be able to walk, so I was incredibly happy. Now she can't run very fast, but she can climb the cat tower and trot, and she walks without dragging her leg, so I'm very grateful.

The prices are reasonable compared to other animal hospitals.

However, the waiting times are too long, and I feel like it's stressing my cat out.

My cat had no appetite. He passed away the day after he was hospitalized. His condition worsened around 11am. I was notified at 8pm. He passed away at 8:30pm, and I missed his last moments. If I had known about his condition from 11am, I would have gone to see him and requested palliative care. I regret that I couldn't. He was gagging and drooling until the very end, and it seems he suffered terribly before he died. It breaks my heart to think that he endured nearly 10 hours of loneliness, anxiety, and suffering all alone from 11am. I wanted to talk to him and hold him in my arms at the end. I don't want animals, who cannot speak, to have to go through this. If your pet suddenly becomes lethargic while hospitalized, please contact the owner as soon as possible to let them know. It's heartbreaking that they had to give him medication to keep his heart beating at the very end. He was a sweet, affectionate, and timid little guy. I wanted to shorten his suffering by even a second.

I have been once here and had the best first experience so far
I took my cat ( Michi) and the doctors were so nice and understanding
I recommend it
The teachers are very helpful, but the receptionist comes across as a bit too businesslike. Their service is professional, though.

My beloved cat kept vomiting, so I rushed her to an emergency vet that night, and was referred to this hospital the next morning.

The tests suggested a possibility of pancreatitis, but it wasn't a definitive diagnosis yet, so I was told to "wait and see for now and come back tomorrow" and sent home.

However, that night she had blood in her urine three times and could barely walk.

I admit I'm partly to blame for not considering another hospital at that point.

The next day, as I was getting ready to go to the hospital first thing in the morning, she passed away.

The vet said, "It's not a matter of life or death today or tomorrow," and "Even if she's not eating, we're giving her IV fluids, so she'll be fine." Believing those words was a mistake.
I trust the doctor 👨‍🏫 and travel all the way from Okayama to have my dog ​​examined. …

The examination and hospitalization took place when my child was in such a critical condition that death could have occurred at any moment. I was crying and panicking, but the doctor calmly and gently explained everything to me. The next day, I was surprised to have to take a patient card and wait even though I was just visiting, but it turned out the doctor was there to explain the situation in detail during my visit. The doctor who had been in charge was off duty, but it seemed they were worried about my child. I had heard that sometimes children pass away in the morning because there are no staff at night, but I also heard that someone stayed behind to look after my child when their condition suddenly worsened during the night.

I had been worried after seeing some negative reviews, but the receptionist was kind, and it was a truly wonderful hospital. Incidentally, people around me also recommend it as a good hospital, so I can vouch for it.

I was so grateful for the consideration shown to me as I was crying and holding my deceased child; they allowed me to pay inside the hospital and leave through the back entrance, and the doctor even saw me off until I turned the corner.

I have many regrets, but I am truly grateful for all the hard work and dedication they put into caring for me in such a short time.

As others have mentioned in their reviews, the reception is terrible 😭 They made mistakes with the vaccination procedures three times in a row, requiring me to come back the same day... and each time they charged me again... and added a rather harsh comment like, "We don't tell you this because it's common sense." She's a well-known receptionist, even featured on their website, but I have a lot of distrust towards them.

I've heard that the doctors vary, and my doctor is very kind and answers all my questions, so I don't want to change hospitals, but the waiting times are awful, and the reception makes serious mistakes quite frequently. I would consider going back if they used AI or an automated reception system instead of those pretty ladies... They are very kind to regulars, like family, so I think the treatment depends on whether they like you or not... 😭

I brought my cat in for cystitis.
I came in wanting antibiotics, but they said we should do some tests.
I said I could afford up to 20,000 yen, and they said it was fine.
They charged me that amount that day, but when I went back another day to get the test results, they added another 20,000 yen, claiming there was a billing error.
What's more, the hospital said there were other bacteria present in their tests, but the external test results showed no bacteria.
You can tell they're profit-driven from the building, but their methods are so dirty.
I don't understand why it's so crowded.

My ferret was diagnosed with malignant lymphoma and was cared for here. He had been in good health, but suddenly started dragging his right leg. I went to my regular doctor, who suggested he might have an insulinoma or a tumor in his spleen. He referred me to another vet. Although all his blood tests, ultrasounds, and X-rays came back normal, I was still concerned, so I requested a CT scan. By chance, a CT scan was available that day, so they performed one right away. After seeing the results, they also performed an MRI. The diagnosis was a tumor in his spine, partially dissolving the bone—a condition that would have been impossible to detect without a CT or MRI. The surgery went smoothly, and although the doctor explained that the surgery would not completely cure him, but would only temporarily relieve the pressure and pain, I agreed to have it performed, as it would make him more comfortable. He was urinating and defecating continuously for about two days before the surgery, which was frightening, but after the surgery, he quickly regained his ability to walk, play with other ferrets, and climb onto the sofa and bed. However, because it was likely malignant, the recurrence was rapid, and he passed away one and a half months after surgery. Although he seemed in a lot of pain before the surgery, his condition changed dramatically from the time of surgery until he passed away. He had no problems urinating or defecating until the very end, and he slowly sank into a coma. If we hadn't had surgery, his end would have been much more tragic. Thanks to finding this hospital, we were able to protect my pet's quality of life until the very end, give us time to prepare ourselves, provide palliative care, and do everything we could to help him. He was even able to lick his favorite treats until the very end.

The reviews of this hospital are divided, both good and bad, but we consider it a miracle that we were able to meet Dr. I. Dr. I encouraged my pet, saying, "Do your best," and treated him with the utmost care. It's clear how much he cares about animals. All the staff were incredibly kind to us during his hospital stay. Since reservations are not possible, there are long wait times, but I can rest assured that if my pet becomes seriously ill, I can leave it to you.
Thanks to the doctors, my pet was able to pass away without any regrets. I am truly grateful. We still have a cat and a ferret, so I think I will continue to rely on you for your care in the future. I would appreciate your continued support.

Recently, I received a CT scan and MRI after being referred from another hospital. My dog ​​had convulsions and needed urgent medical attention, so luckily there was an available MRI slot available, allowing for the test and treatment to be performed that same day.

Dr. Kido examined my dog ​​first, and he greeted my dog ​​first, which made me very happy.

The MRI results showed an intranasal tumor that had leaked into the skull, causing brain herniation and a risk of sudden death.

The doctor carefully explained the MRI results to me, and he listened attentively to my concerns about the poor prognosis, treatment options, and treatments that might be best avoided.

He is currently receiving palliative care, but his condition is stable.

I was a little worried after reading reviews, but I was able to see a good doctor, so I'm glad I went. I'm not sure if doctors are good or bad, but I think it depends on the compatibility between the owner and the dog, the condition of the illness or injury, and how busy they are at the time.

The nurses were also cheerful and kind.

My dog ​​was feeling unwell so I went to the emergency room. It's extremely crowded on weekends and you can't make a reservation.
There's a parking lot, but if it's full you'll have to use the multi-story car park.
I get the impression that doctors change frequently.
The prices are a bit high
This hospital is an indispensable place for pet owners and their pets. Thank you to everyone who works there.

The woman who answered the phone the last time I called was very nice, but when I called today at 9:30, the woman's attitude was extremely bad and made me feel bad. I've been using this hospital for a long time, so I hope they improve their reception service soon. The doctors are very nice, but the customer service attitude of some of the women at the reception desk is unpleasant.

Since the clinic's reception time was just around the corner, I headed straight from work, checked in first, and left to return with my pet. When I got home, I received a call. I explained the situation and was told to postpone the appointment until tomorrow. I told them I'd be back in five or ten minutes, but they put me on hold, so I hung up and hurried on my way. Upon arriving, the main entrance was closed, so I called again and was told to postpone it until tomorrow. I insisted, "I checked in within the designated time, and there were still a few people waiting, right?" They told me, "We called you immediately after checking in. If you want to see the doctor, there will be an after-hours fee" (5,000 yen). I had no choice but to accept the appointment, but is this a government office? Was I charged an after-hours fee for being away for only 10 minutes? I have no intention of criticizing the doctor, and I'll continue to go there because it's close, but asking me to postpone the appointment until tomorrow when there are suffering animals is a cold-hearted hospital that doesn't care about the lives or the feelings of pet owners.
I believe the veterinarians are of a certain level, but for a long time, the reception staff have been surprisingly incompetent, which has been unpleasant for many people.

My hamster broke a bone, so I had the head veterinarian perform surgery. There are very few hospitals in Osaka that can perform surgery on hamsters, but thanks to the thorough examination and surgery, my hamster has recovered to the point where it can run around again. I'm so glad I entrusted my hamster to the doctor.☺️ It's a large hospital, so it can get quite crowded, but I recommend getting a numbered ticket before it opens to shorten your waiting time.

Before, they would immediately see animals in life-threatening situations that required immediate attention.
Now, even if there's an animal in danger, they pretend not to see it.
I think if they did the same thing to a human, it would be the same as letting them die.
While I was being examined today, I could see the dire situation of the pets of other people who were there.
It was painful to watch, but they didn't see them immediately. I think they should at least put the animal on a ventilator until the examination. Even if they charged for that, the owners wouldn't get angry.
The facilities are certainly good, but I wish they would reconsider the importance of life.

I learned about Dr. Tatsumi from watching him on TV a few years ago.

He treated my pet's patellar luxation, which my local veterinary hospital had said was incurable.

He's a doctor who explains things very carefully.

Even now, my pet is hospitalized because he wasn't getting proper care at my local hospital and nearly died.

I have multiple pets in Shiga Prefecture, and I rely on him whenever something comes up.

They were very kind and the treatment was appropriate.

I am grateful that you saved my life.

I will never forgive this hospital. Absolutely not.

I want a full refund.

I don't care about the sullen receptionist.

I have two cats. My older cat became ill, and although they gave her IV fluids and X-rays, they showed no willingness to compromise on the cause.

They casually said things like, "Please observe her for a week without food or water," and

The medication they prescribed didn't help at all.

I rushed her to the emergency room, and after explaining the treatment, they finally explained everything in detail and I understood.

I found a different hospital, and my regular vet there is very thorough and kind.

Thanks to them, she has truly recovered and is healthy again. I'm so glad.

How dare they say "observe her for a week" after the examination?

All they do is have rules, you can't even get an appointment, and then they give you a haphazard diagnosis? Before I found my current vet, I called and said, "My cat isn't getting better. What should I do?"

They said, "You can't get an appointment, so you have to come in."


They only give similar examinations; what exactly are they trying to cure?
I've visited this clinic multiple times and seen three different doctors regarding this issue.
It's truly awful.

My beloved cat, who had cardiomyopathy, was treated by Dr. Shibata for about five months.

She suddenly became lethargic, and when I took her to the vet, cardiomyopathy was discovered, and I was told she didn't have long to live. However, thanks to the doctor's and Fuku-chan's efforts, we were able to spend five precious months together. ✨
Thanks to the careful examination and diagnosis, Fuku-chan had a good appetite and remained energetic until the very end, and I believe she was able to live happily without suffering.

It was clear that he loves animals, and he was a very kind doctor who was gentle and supportive of pet owners.

I couldn't express my gratitude properly over the phone, so I'm taking this opportunity to thank him.

The previous director, Dr. Ogura, was a very good doctor and I trusted him, but I hear he has retired.

I used to go to Dr. Hige when he was the director of Fukushima Central Animal Hospital, a group hospital, and I wrote a detailed review about him there, but he seriously misdiagnosed both my rescued kitten and my existing Pomeranian, so I never want Dr. Hige to treat my pet again.

I went to this hospital because it was well-equipped and I trusted Dr. Ogura, but now that Dr. Ogura is gone, there's no point in coming here anymore.

At the local animal hospital, they always said the cause was unknown even after tests and only prescribed symptomatic medication, so I couldn't rely on them at all. However, when I saw Dr. Ogura, the cause was usually determined, so I felt safe coming here, and now I'm at a loss as to where to take my pet if something happens in the future...

I had brought my dog ​​to Osaka Animal Medical Center, thinking that a large, well-equipped hospital would provide thorough care. However, as I researched animal hospitals, I found that none of the doctors at this hospital hold any of the following specialized qualifications:

[Japanese Certified Veterinary Oncologist]

[Japanese Society of Veterinary Nephrology and Urology Certified Doctor]

[Japanese Society of Veterinary Cardiology Certified Doctor]

[Japanese Small Animal Surgeon]

[Veterinary Ophthalmologist]
... Nowadays, some veterinary clinics offer consultations by specialists in fields such as oncology, cardiology, and ophthalmology. If anything were to happen in the future, I'd first have my pet taken to a nearby veterinary clinic for blood tests and other tests to narrow down the possible causes. Then, I'd consult a specialist based on the symptoms, such as a certified oncologist if a tumor is suspected, or a certified nephrologist/urologist if the kidneys seem to be involved.

By the way, here's how to find certified doctors:

- Japanese Society of Veterinary Oncology

- Japanese Society of Veterinary Nephrology and Urology

- Japanese Society of Veterinary Cardiology

- Japanese Association of Small Animal Surgeons

- Japanese Society of Comparative Ophthalmology

Each of the above websites lists certified doctors nationwide, but they don't seem to be designed for patients to search. For example, the Japanese Society of Veterinary Nephrology and Urology doesn't break down by prefecture, and just lists the names of certified doctors and veterinary clinics, making it quite difficult to find a hospital within commuting distance. (I repeatedly entered the doctor's name and the name of the veterinary clinic and searched...lol.)

First of all, the waiting times are incredibly long. There were days when I had to stay there all day. And even though I was seeing the same doctor every time, they didn't keep track of what medications I was taking or anything like that.

Also, I bought a two-month supply of medication, but when I checked at home, there was only a one-month supply. I've had problems with medication multiple times.

I feel like I need to change hospitals soon.

My cats are being taken care of there.
The level of busyness varies from day to day.
Even on Sundays, if you come first thing in the morning, you can be finished by noon.
It really depends on the type of examination.
There seem to be mixed opinions about it, but you won't know until you check it out.

We treated him from October 2024 to April 2025. 🐱 We found a wonderful doctor
and he was always available for appointments.
Not knowing when our final farewell would come,
we found this hospital, and he survived for six months. 🐈‍⬛
In April, he passed away and went to the Rainbow Bridge.
I called the hospital to express my gratitude.
The doctor who took care of him was also very busy, so I was able to thank him over the phone.

A few days later, I received a delivery from the hospital.

I wondered what it was, and when I opened it, I found flowers.

I was so happy I couldn't stop crying.

I'm so glad we found this hospital and this doctor. Thanks to this hospital and my beloved cat's hard work, he survived for six months.

Thank you so much.

Please be careful, everyone.
Just because it's an animal medical center doesn't mean it has the necessary facilities, and the doctors don't provide thorough examinations. My cat was diagnosed with anemia by my family doctor around mid-August, and I was referred to this hospital where Dr. K is examining him. My cat had lost all energy and appetite, so they kept doing tests every time. They kept doing blood tests even though he was anemic. I even suggested a blood transfusion during my initial consultation. It finally happened last week, on August 22nd, when he was scheduled for a transfusion. The morning before, he became ill, so I contacted the hospital, but they couldn't do anything. They coldly told me to look elsewhere. A few minutes later, my cat passed away. It had only been a few days since I'd been to the hospital. They said the initial consultation didn't indicate a serious condition, and they only performed tests for the next few days. I imagine it must have been exhausting, with no IV drips. Even though he was anemic, they still had to draw his blood every time. Of course, it would be exhausting if he didn't have enough blood to begin with, right? That was your mistake, wasn't it? I was shocked that they ultimately told me to look elsewhere. I was abandoned, wasn't I? I'm sure my life could have been saved, so I only regret coming to this hospital. Please be careful not to end up in the same position.

July 20th... We will never forget this day in our lives.

This is the day my precious, precious child lost their life due to a misdiagnosis by an ignorant, incompetent, and unpleasant female doctor at this hospital.
It has been a painful and difficult year.
What is even more unforgivable is the hospital director's response afterward. Since that day, our time has been stopped, and we will never be freed from that nightmarish and painful experience.
I will never forgive them.
I haven't come to terms with it yet, but one day I will definitely post the letter I received from this ridiculous hospital.
Don't be fooled by the hospital's media and facilities.
I recommend choosing an animal hospital with a full staff of specialists.
Also, I do not recommend female veterinarians.
Even though we asked for an experienced and trustworthy doctor, she took time off because our child had a fever, and didn't seem to be taking the examination seriously at all.
I don't know if they are still at this hospital, but that's the level of care they provide. You can't entrust the life of your precious family member to them. From reading the comments, it seems there are many people in the same situation as us.
I sincerely hope that no more lives will be lost due to inexperienced and irresponsible treatment.
I am posting this because my review was deleted. Unforgivable
Age 6, Miniature Pinscher

I've been coming to this clinic for a certain symptom for about a year and a half.
I was told from the beginning that surgery would cure me, so I kept asking them to perform the surgery, but they just said to wait and see, and just when I thought they'd finally given the OK to perform the surgery, they revised the fees and the price went up significantly.
It's really tough to be turned down for some unknown reason, even though they suggested surgery would cure me, and then the price went up.
I asked them to perform the surgery every time I went to the clinic...

The staff were polite, didn't perform any unnecessary tests, and listened to what I had to say while explaining the necessary tests and medications. The staff were also very kind to my dog, so I felt at ease leaving him in their care.

The other day, my parakeet accidentally swallowed some metal and suddenly started vomiting and not eating, so I took him to the hospital. However, I was told, "There's a chance he won't survive, so be prepared," and was given almost no treatment options, which left me feeling very hopeless.
After that, we went to another hospital, and after a week in the hospital, he's now regaining his strength and is slowly recovering.
I was deeply saddened by the way they gave up on a bird's life so easily, and I would never recommend this to pet owners who care for their birds.

On the morning of July 2nd, my beloved dog suddenly lost the use of its hind legs. I took it to another animal hospital where it was diagnosed with a herniated disc.

On July 3rd, desperate for treatment, I visited Osaka Animal Medical Center.

After further examination, it was diagnosed with progressive myelomalacia.

Still unable to believe it, I consulted another hospital, but they also advised against surgery and recommended pain relief methods.

Afterward, I continued caring for it at home for several days, but its condition steadily worsened, leaving it almost bedridden, and it began experiencing occasional respiratory distress.

My husband and I discussed it and decided to let it rest before its condition deteriorated further. We returned to the hospital and opted for euthanasia.

Thanks to Dr. Araki, who was in charge of the case, for his frank explanation of the diagnosis, we were given time to decide on future courses of action.

Thank you for your understanding and support when we requested euthanasia.

Furthermore, I was deeply grateful for the extended time we were given to say goodbye on the day of the procedure, for the beautiful angel care performed on my dog, and for the thoughtful consideration shown by everyone until we left the hospital.

Thank you so much for everything.

This is the third time we've received care here. Each time, we were referred here by a hospital near our home.

Normally, we went to the nearby hospital for checkups.

At the nearby hospital, we had previously expressed our wish to avoid surgery if possible, as our dog is 12 years old and had undergone two surgeries since turning 9. We knew that surgery would be a significant burden if the dog developed a difficult-to-cure illness like a tumor. Around December 2023, our dog experienced persistent vomiting but was otherwise healthy and eating, so we decided to monitor him without blood tests. In late December, the vomiting didn't stop, so we performed blood tests and an ultrasound. His kidney values ​​were elevated, and although we tried medication, there was no improvement. Another blood test revealed abnormally high levels, including inflammation, and he also developed jaundice, which is when we brought him to this hospital. His inflammation and other values ​​were quite bad, making surgery impossible. However, he was admitted that day and underwent intensive medical treatment for several days. After his values ​​improved slightly, a CT scan revealed a stone blockage, causing bile duct obstruction and gallbladder rupture. After the surgery, ascites accumulated and other problems arose, but we were able to be discharged safely. We were hospitalized for a total of over 60 days. During that time, the doctors and nurses were very kind and caring, and of course the reception staff were also very nice. We were able to go home. Thank you so much. Now we visit the clinic once a month. Although many grooming salons refuse to groom our dog due to its age, this salon does grooming for us. The combination of clinic visits and grooming is a great help.

The atmosphere inside the hospital has changed a lot over the past year or so. First of all, the waiting time is now around 0 to 20 minutes no matter when I go. Secondly, the female receptionists are extremely brusque and their cliched speeches seem to be getting more and more unpleasant. As for the actual examination, I no longer feel half of the confidence, insight and sincerity that I naturally felt from the previous veterinarians and nurses. Also, the consultation fees seem to be much higher than the amount posted on the wall of the examination room.
When there are serious problems with management or personnel, the reputation and atmosphere can change drastically, and this happens not only in hospitals but in any organization. Proper equipment is essential to the quality of medical care, so rather than looking for another hospital, I would rather they go back to being a crowded place like before.

The hospital looked big and impressive, but in reality it wasn't very good. My dog ​​suffered from stomach pains and went to the hospital for six months, even undergoing surgery, but there was no improvement. They just prescribed steroids. After that, we changed to another hospital and he finally recovered.

Just because a hospital looks impressive and has well-equipped facilities doesn't necessarily mean the quality of medical care is high. Especially with animals, the level of care and experience they provide is very important.

My dog ​​had been suffering from stomach pains for six months and even underwent surgery, so I wonder if the diagnosis was correct and the treatment plan appropriate. Fortunately, he finally got better after changing hospitals, which is really great.
The waiting room is spacious and clean, and the doctor is kind.

I went there around 8 PM thinking they were still offering emergency services at night, but they said they hadn't done so since March. I understand that they must have had their reasons for stopping the emergency service, but when I asked, "Are there any other emergency hospitals nearby?", they didn't even make eye contact and just said, "Oh, I don't know." It was such a heartless response, and it's terrifying to think that people like that are involved in caring for animal lives.

When my cat swallowed some string, I went to another hospital and they told me I'd have to have an abdominal surgery, but that wasn't the case! Thank you so much! 😊
I'll definitely be coming here from now on! And I'm so glad you were my doctor!

Since reservations aren't possible, you'll have to wait about two hours even if you go early. I think it's one of the best animal medical facilities in Osaka. There's also a multi-story parking garage, so there's plenty of space for cars.

Don't assume a hospital is safe just because it's big or has great facilities. The veterinarians themselves are often completely lacking. It's just big! It's famous because it's been in the media! Can you really entrust the life of your precious family member to a veterinarian who's overconfident and deluded just because they work in such a place? Choosing the right hospital is truly important. I hope that as many people as possible don't have to go through the same thing.

My cat had an epileptic seizure and I rushed her to the vet at night, but the receptionist told me that we would have to wait if an emergency patient came in. I said, "But it *is* an emergency!" and only then did they finally put her in the oxygen chamber. My cat, who wasn't considered an emergency patient, passed away a week later. I think this hospital is incapable of being supportive of pet owners and their animals.

I wouldn't even give it a 1.

Misdiagnosis error. They said the cause was unknown and prescribed medication.

I got a second opinion, and the prescribed medication was ineffective. My symptoms were so severe that the cause was clearly identifiable.

Are you a new doctor?

What do you think of human life?

What do you mean, "cause unknown"?

The consultation fee is just expensive.

There's no point in going.

The receptionist is unpleasant.

Seeing her perfectly manicured nails is a turn-off.

Well, I suppose the receptionist isn't involved in the examination.

They even returned my pet carrier to someone else, and there are many other things that bother me.

I only go there because it's a large hospital with good facilities.

A blood test revealed that my cat's leg claw was broken at the base.
I've taken my cats and dogs to the hospital many times, but this is the first time something like this has happened.

My 9-year-old cat has lost his appetite.

I came to this hospital a few years ago for urinary stones, so I wanted to ask about food.

He had trouble getting into his carrier, and going to the hospital is stressful for him.

He's a scaredy-cat, so please try not to hurt him! I told the doctor.

The blood test was over in less than 10 minutes, and when I returned,

the nurse brought the broken claw back.

"It looks like the claw is broken, so if the bleeding doesn't stop, please come back tomorrow. The Elizabethan collar is still on, so please bring it back."

I couldn't understand what she meant.

My cat was still wearing its collar and was meowing like crazy in its carrier,
and I was completely puzzled as to why its claw had broken at the base. When I asked the doctor about the cause and circumstances of the broken claw,
he said that after taking a blood sample and clipping its nails, he put it back in the carrier,
and then it panicked and climbed about a meter up the wall, and that's when it probably broke.

The blood test results came back clean, so I was relieved,

but in the end, he said that the broken claw might belong to a different cat.

He said that even if we put a bandage on it, it would probably come off,

so just to be safe, he prescribed antibiotics and painkillers and sent me home.

When I got home, my cat was covered in blood and
he was hiding under the sofa, cowering in fear.

It looked like the claw on its left hind paw was broken, and it was walking as if it was protecting itself.

The doctor explained that it was because it was trying to climb the wall, so how could a hind paw break? I wasn't convinced, so I called the next day, but they gave me the same explanation: they didn't break it on purpose, but my pet panicked and started acting violently.

I was concerned because there was no explanation about the side effects of the prescribed antibiotics and painkillers, so I looked them up online the next day and found that these strong medications often cause vomiting and loss of appetite in pets, so I ended up not giving them the medicine.

A week has passed and my pet's appetite has improved considerably, but there are still days when he won't eat, so it's not stable.

I imagine that my pet, who can't speak, was scared and in pain when the inconsiderate doctor and amateurish staff forcefully held him down to clip his nails and draw his blood, and I regret going to this hospital, as I feel that all my efforts were wasted.

The blood test results were normal, but they couldn't determine the reason for his lack of appetite and energy, and he was sent back with an injury, so I'm really frustrated and dissatisfied.
It takes time, but it's a great veterinary clinic.
I took my frog in when it wasn't feeling well. They assessed its age and gave me advice, and it gradually recovered after using the prescribed medication. Thank you so much!

My 13-year-old cat had terminal cancer.

We were told that she would suffocate if the fluid in her chest wasn't drained, so we were taking her to this hospital twice a week.

I begged them to let me care for her until the end, but they told me to go to a nearby hospital. However, when I went to the nearby hospital, it was closed and they couldn't see her.
There was nothing I could do, and the next day, on the way to the nearby hospital, she passed away in the car.

Even though her life couldn't be saved, if they had been able to care for her until the end, we could have spent a few more weeks together.
The clinic is clean. It's bright and has a clean feel to it.

Our three hedgehogs have been cared for by Dr. Tatsumi, the head veterinarian, for over four years.

In recent years, they've suffered from all sorts of illnesses.

He always provided clear and easy-to-understand explanations, and considered treatment plans with the owner's feelings in mind.

As a doctor who has treated many exotic animals, he was able to quickly diagnose even rare diseases, never recommending unnecessary tests or surgeries, and always thinking of treatment methods that would alleviate my anxieties, saying things like, "If it were my hedgehog, this is what I would do!" He's a very kind doctor.

Even when I hesitated to put my little ones under anesthesia, Dr. Tatsumi's reassuring words put me at ease.

During examinations, he spoke to even the hedgehogs, who aren't usually friendly, in a gentle tone, praised them, and handled them carefully, which made me feel warm and happy just watching him.

I always knew that if I had any concerns, I could always rely on Dr. Tatsumi, and even though hedgehogs have short lifespans, I believe it's thanks to Dr. Tatsumi that I was able to spend about five years with him.

Thank you so much for saving my beloved pets.

I am truly grateful to have met Dr. Tatsumi and that he was our primary veterinarian.

At the end of last year, after the 49th day memorial service for our last pet who passed away, I was gradually coming to terms with the loss when you sent flowers, which filled my heart with even more gratitude.

If I ever have the opportunity to welcome another pet into my life, I would definitely want Dr. Tatsumi to examine them, so I hope you will take care of them then as well.
The wait time is long, but it's reliable and beautiful.

It was completely useless at the most important moment. 
Unfortunately, I don't think I'll be visiting again.
This place is no good.

There used to be a very trustworthy veterinarian here, but I guess good doctors leave because they don't like the way this hospital does things! Now, it seems like they're just going through the motions, lacking knowledge and a sense of responsibility as veterinarians who deal with lives... My pet died from a misdiagnosis due to such a veterinarian. The hospital director says on YouTube that there shouldn't be any misdiagnoses or medical errors, but... the reviews are full of misdiagnoses! Don't trust the superficial, flimsy positive reviews that try to cover up the bad ones. Look carefully at the 1-star reviews and think about what you would do if your own pet went through that. I don't want anyone else to go through the same thing! I also can't forgive this hospital for deleting reviews written by people who can't forgive what happened to them. Is it for the hospital's reputation? Do they want to hide it? My posts have been deleted many times, but I keep posting them so that as many people as possible can see them before they're deleted again. There's not a shred of sincerity! Animals have lives too. They're not objects. They're family. It's not something that can be settled with just an apology. I will remember what was done to me for the rest of my life.

Our dogs have been receiving care here for many years. We feel at ease because they can perform tests using the latest equipment that other hospitals don't offer. The vet in charge doesn't perform unnecessary tests or prescribe unnecessary medications, and if he's unsure about something, he'll clearly tell us what he would do.

I was treated for my kitten's accidental ingestion. All of the doctors were kind and polite.
X-rays and ultrasounds couldn't find the cause, so they even performed a CT scan, which revealed the kitten had accidentally ingested something.
We didn't have insurance, so the initial X-ray and ultrasound cost just over 30,000 yen, followed by a CT scan and endoscopy. Even those couldn't remove the substance, so the total cost for the laparotomy and four days of hospitalization came to just over 170,000 yen. Thanks to their efforts, the kitten returned home healthy and well!
The day we visited was Christmas morning, so it was relatively quiet, but it was quite busy on other days.

Dr. Akamatsu's explanations and approach are very easy to understand, and I'm always grateful for his help.

I think this is a hospital where you can feel at ease.
I have my pet meerkat examined here. There is also a dog grooming salon.

The doctor explained everything carefully.
I wish I had come here from the beginning.
There is a contracted parking lot, so it is easy to get to.

There are probably places where treatment costs are cheaper, but they may not have CT equipment or you may have to go to a different hospital, so it may take a while to be seen.

They have great facilities so they can look at everything.

I'm sure many people are concerned about the cost, but now I think it would have been better to have pet insurance.
When your pet is young, they're healthy and rarely go to the hospital, but once they're over 10 years old, you'll probably have to go to the hospital more often, so I think it's best to get insurance as soon as you can.
I think it's best to have as few worries as possible other than illness and injury.
I'm glad I found such a great teacher.

My dog's life was also taken by this hospital's misdiagnosis, which could have been saved.
My dog ​​had a loss of appetite, so we took him to a nearby veterinary clinic. They diagnosed his kidney numbers as poor and recommended that we take him to a better-equipped hospital, so we took him there and asked them to take him to their clinic, where they diagnosed him with kidney problems.
The diagnosis was acute pancreatitis.
They said his kidney numbers weren't that bad.
Because his pancreatic numbers were bad, they said he would get better if he received a pancreatic infusion every week. Feeling completely relieved, we went back every day for the infusion, but we explained that he still wasn't getting better and asked them to examine his kidneys again. When we returned, they diagnosed him with a misdiagnosis. They found a tumor in his kidney and there was nothing they could do! I'm so sorry.
Don't be ridiculous! That's why I told you from the beginning that he had kidney problems and wanted them to take him in for a checkup! And the instructions on the medication said that the infusion shouldn't be given to dogs with kidney problems.
I completely lost faith in them and took them to another hospital, but they said if we'd just taken him a little earlier, they'd have treated him!
No matter how well-equipped the facilities are, it's pointless if the veterinarian is this level. I should have done more research on the hospital. I blame myself every day for taking my dog ​​to this hospital.
I'm sure this review will be deleted, but this is the truth about what happened to us at this hospital.
This female doctor is still working there, unconcerned.
I can't even begin to describe it all here. I will never forgive her.

My dog ​​was misdiagnosed at this hospital and died the next day at the age of three.

I rushed him in because he was vomiting violently, but after numerous tests, I was told things like, "Maybe the food isn't right for him?"

The treatment was done behind the scenes, out of sight, and while I paid, I was told, "That's all. Take care." When I told them I hadn't been given my dog ​​back, they said, "We forgot."

Is it even possible for a hospital to be like that?

He died the day after the misdiagnosis at the age of three.

A second opinion revealed pulmonary edema, but it was too late.

Despite that, I keep receiving postcards asking if I want to buy heartworm medication for my deceased dog.

I regret going to this hospital so much that I could cry.

They appear on TV and such, but there's a tremendous difference in experience among the veterinarians.

I hope no more dogs lose their lives.

My beloved 15-year-old dog suffered from various illnesses, but Dr. A and the nurses treated her with love and care day and night. Although she eventually passed away, our whole family was able to be there to see her off.

We are truly grateful.

My dog ​​had fluid buildup in his lungs, possibly due to aspiration, and for a while I was worried about his condition, but he was saved.

Where is Dr. Shindo, who treated us so well, practicing now?

He was such a good doctor, and I felt sorry for him after seeing some negative reviews from other patients.

They say the best doctor is the one who sees you later, and I think this clinic can be a place where a doctor becomes a great doctor after seeing someone later, and vice versa. In the process of running the clinic, it's inevitable that some incompetent veterinarians and receptionists will join. And sometimes you'll end up with one of them. You just have to go into the clinic with the understanding that timing and luck are not entirely absent. If you want to eliminate those factors, I think it's better to go to a clinic with only one doctor. So far, I think people who haven't encountered such veterinarians or receptionists will give it a high rating, and those who have will give it a low rating. Personally, I give it a high rating. However, I've heard stories of dogs that were being monitored with medication elsewhere, but the cause was identified here, and although it had progressed somewhat, they were saved by surgery, and there are also the opposite stories in the reviews here.
The doctors and nurses are all very kind.

The clinic is very clean and has a hygienic feel.

All the staff are very kind.

I heard this place had good facilities, so I took my pet there the other day, but I felt like it was treated very roughly. Looking at the reviews, they're awful! Whenever a bad review is posted, a good one immediately pops up... the hospital is desperate to keep its rating down!

I regret not checking the reviews beforehand. Being a large hospital or having good facilities is completely irrelevant. I think local veterinary clinics are far superior in terms of experience and how they treat their animals. I will never go there again, but I sincerely hope that as many cats and dogs as possible can be saved.

I paid a high fee at this well-equipped center, and the diagnosis showed nothing abnormal, and the doctor was young. After that, the condition did not change, so I went to my usual local hospital, where they diagnosed him with a foreign object through palpation, and immediately performed surgery, and a lump of rubber came out. It was an animal center that couldn't even diagnose something like that. I never want to go there again.
If you're a member, treatment costs are halved. That's a huge help.

I was looking for a hospital for my dog, but after reading the reviews here, I realized I shouldn't take him there. The positive reviews only suggest the hospital is fabricating the case, and it seems they won't take responsibility for any medical errors. I'm glad I read the reviews before taking him.

I don't understand why this post was deleted, but do they delete posts that are inconvenient for the hospital?

Just like humans, when animals get sick, the only place they can rely is the hospital.

There may be good veterinarians, but it's also true that there are veterinarians who easily take irreplaceable lives through misdiagnosis and then continue working as if nothing happened.

Even if they take the life of my precious family member, under this country's law, it's merely property damage! I want people to understand that there are hospitals that use lives to make money with such an attitude.

What pet owners can do is to keep a record of the detailed explanations they receive during examinations, such as what injections will be given and what medications will be prescribed. This will definitely be useful when the worst happens. Dogs and cats don't understand words! No matter what happens, they trust their owners! Please don't forget that.

After visiting two other hospitals, there was no sign of recovery.
We then visited this clinic through the breeder, and the results showed that a condition that hadn't been diagnosed at the other two hospitals was discovered. An additional medication was prescribed, and we saw gradual improvement the next day, followed by a remarkable recovery the following day. I am now convinced that this doctor is truly the best for bushbabies.

I have a tumor and have received chemotherapy three times, and it's currently ongoing. There were times when I was worried that I wouldn't make it, but I'm gradually regaining my strength.

I'm also gaining weight, which makes me very happy.

I still have to continue going to the hospital, but I'm truly grateful to the doctor.

On October 13th, I took my dog ​​to a hospital near my home because they found a lump in its mouth. They said it needed immediate surgery and only had about a month to live, or at the earliest, a week later depending on their schedule. My friend recommended the Osaka Animal Medical Center, so I rushed there. The result was malignant melanoma. After discussing it with my regular vet, we decided on chemotherapy every other day to slow metastasis. I went back every two weeks for checkups to monitor for chemotherapy and metastasis, but my regular vet was on vacation. They asked if another vet would be alright, but since the chemotherapy had run out, I went to Dr. Hige. I explained the examination, the tests for metastasis, and anything that had changed in the past two weeks. He prescribed medication to give once a day, so I went home. About 15 minutes after giving the medication, my dog ​​had a seizure, and I rushed back to the hospital near my home. Of course, I brought the prescribed medication with me and showed it to him.

"Well, I wouldn't prescribe that," he said.
I went back to the Osaka Animal Medical Center, where he prescribed the medication, and spoke with Dr. Hige again.

To put it simply, he said, "I'm confident in the medication I prescribed."

I won't lose no matter where I'm taken.

Those words made me take a breather.

I was asked if there had been any seizures since then, but I just said that side effects from the medication are rare in any dog. Since I brought my dog ​​in, Dr. Hige was worried, and since it was the first time, he said he would honestly give the dog the medicine Dr. Hige prescribed, and that he would be happy to see the dog, but there would be a consultation fee. Dr. Hige seems to appear on YouTube, so I understand his confidence, but a doctor who truly saves dogs' lives should talk to the owner later and then ask if it's okay to see the dog first because they're worried. Of course, he said there would be a consultation fee. The police came too, and wow, there are doctors like this, even if it's rare.

If Dr. Hige is reading this comment, since you're a doctor at an animal medical center, I hope you'll think about this seriously and never make the mistake of causing another dog to suffer again. I'm terrified of Dr. Hige misdiagnosing me at that hospital, so you should admit your mistakes a little; that would give you room for improvement.

Learn more.

Dr. Hige

I take my dog ​​here for checkups.
All the veterinarians are kind and helpful, and the clinic has a variety of facilities, which gives me peace of mind.
The reception staff are also friendly.
There's often a long wait, but I suppose that's unavoidable since it's a popular clinic.

It's a popular hospital, but there's a difference depending on the doctor.

I think I'll avoid Dr. T.
I've been coming here ever since I was referred. The doctors and nurses are so kind to me, I feel at ease when I visit.
It's a very clean hospital with many doctors and friendly staff. However, it's always crowded because it's popular, so waiting is inevitable (^^;;

I own an unusual pet, and there are few hospital options available. However, Dr. Tatsumi here is full of love for animals, and he doesn't perform unnecessary tests that unnecessarily stress the animals, so I feel at ease bringing my pet here.

Even for the initial consultation, another hospital quoted me 100,000 yen per animal, requiring vaccinations and all sorts of tests under general anesthesia. Here, however, they only require a visual examination, palpation, and a consultation with the owner. I'm afraid of hospitals that unnecessarily put small animals under general anesthesia or administer vaccinations.

I can't imagine going to any other hospital.

Some people occasionally write about long waiting times, but seeing how diligently Dr. Tatsumi focuses on my pet and quickly performs only the necessary procedures, I believe he treats all other animals just as diligently and quickly, so it's not a problem at all.

Other veterinarians don't seem to be able to treat the exotic animals I own, so I don't know about the other veterinarians mentioned in other reviews, but I would be lost without Dr. Tatsumi.

I am always so grateful for your thorough care.

I have been under the care of the head doctor for 13 years. …
